title: Mercy, not sacrifice (Matthew 9:1–13)
hook: go and learn what this means, quoting Hosea 6:6
tomorrow: what happens when two people need him at once?

segments.voice: Yesterday a storm obeyed and a town asked him to leave. Your line: what manner of man. Now he's back across the water.

Mid-argument in a comment section, someone types: read the actual article first. Matthew's version comes at a dinner. Jesus has called a man from the tax booth with two words, follow me, and the man "arose, and followed him." Now the table fills with tax collectors and people the town calls sinners. Some Pharisees, teachers devoted to keeping God's law, ask the disciples a real question: "Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?" Jesus answers with homework.
screen: `READ THE ARTICLE FIRST.` → `A TABLE FULL OF PUBLICANS.` → `A REAL QUESTION.`

segments.voice: "They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice." Go and learn sends people back to a text they already share: the prophet Hosea, scripture for Jesus and the Pharisees alike. "For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings." So this is an argument inside one Bible about what it puts first. Christians read the line two ways, and both deserve a hearing. One view hears instead of: what God wants is kindness, not ceremony, and any rule that keeps the sick from the doctor has missed the point. The other view hears more than: look at Hosea's second half, the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. That's a ranking, not a ban. Worship stays; mercy goes first. The first view asks: what's a ritual worth if it shuts someone out? The second answers: the same scripture asks for both, in the right order. Both agree on the table. Matthew even opens the page with a man on a bed hearing, "Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee." Mercy comes first in both scenes.
screen: `GO AND LEARN.` · `HOSEA: MERCY, NOT SACRIFICE.` · `VIEW ONE: INSTEAD OF.` · `VIEW TWO: MORE THAN.` · then, large: `MERCY, NOT SACRIFICE.`

segments.voice: Name one disagreement where being right has started to matter more than the person. Picture the obstacle, the line you always want to win with; then choose one plain, merciful move for the next time it comes up, and hold it as you breathe.
Mercy. What Hosea says God desires, quoted by Jesus at a table full of the wrong guests.
Pocket this one: mercy, not sacrifice, or mercy first, and both readings start at the table. See you tomorrow.

fork.setup: you've always heard mercy, not sacrifice as mercy instead of worship. state the other reading at its strongest.
options: Hosea's next words, more than burnt offerings, rank them: mercy first, worship kept.
sacrifice meant giving up treats, so Jesus says skip self-denial.

fork.reveal: Hosea 6:6: I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. the second view hears a ranking, not a ban. both views agree on the dinner.

original.note: Greek: mercy, the word in Matthew 9:13 where Jesus quotes Hosea.

trapdoor: what you thought: mercy, not sacrifice means rituals don't matter.
what it means: Hosea weighs two good things and says God desires mercy more; Jesus quotes it to explain who sits at his table.

chat.says: Aunt Jo says Dale at Pop's party = drama. "keep the peace, it's Pop's day." who's right??
options: Mercy first, for Dale and for Aunt Jo too. Hosea weighs good things; nobody has to win.
Aunt Jo. Jesus kept people with a past away from big family dinners to keep the peace.
You. Mercy means no rules at all, so Aunt Jo's worries don't count for anything.
chat.meaning: Jesus said go and learn: I will have mercy, and not sacrifice. Hosea weighs good things and puts mercy first, for everyone at the table.

Pharisees.meaning: a Jewish group devoted to keeping God's law closely

Hosea.meaning: a prophet of Israel whose words Jesus quotes

burnt offerings.meaning: sacrifices burned whole on the altar
